sources: dossier=Net position line 14 (2026-06-20..21, transcript): 'cascade among holders continues during the hold; the deferred commit/abandon cascade fires only to non-members'; corrections line 72 (transcript): the sketch's blanket defer-all-cascade was corrected because holders must keep cascading during the hold; doc=claim-handle.md:58 (was line 56) and :68 (was line 66) asserted the held transition fires no cascade and downstream sees terminal/success only at Commit; code=runner_terminal.go:197-231 fires a member-filtered terminal/success + attribute-change walk at running->held, before Commit
note: Doc over-broadly denied any cascade at the held transition; dossier (transcript tier) establishes the member-filtered cascade during hold is intentional, with only the non-member walk deferred to auto-terminal. Corrected doc to state the member-directed cascade fires immediately and only the non-member walk is deferred.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 29 (2026-05-17, artifact): 'SweepClaimHandleRetention reaps committed-subgraph and abandoned rows past retention... must never delete durable-committed rows'; doc=claim-handle.md line 18 said durable rows are reaped only by explicit Release (overstated) and line 44's filter description said 'committed-or-abandoned' (understated, ambiguous vs durable-committed exemption); line 67 already stated the exemption correctly, creating an internal contradiction; code=postgres/sqlite claim_handles.go DELETE predicate confirmed
note: Doc contradicted itself: one line correctly scoped the retention-sweep exemption to committed-durable rows, two others didn't. Dossier's own retention-sweep description matches the correct line. Fixed the two incorrect lines to match.

sources: dossier=Net position line 18 (2026-05-28, artifact): 'terminate makes the instance terminal and abandons uncommitted in-flight claims'; Intentional absences line 60: durable release stays DELETE's job, not terminate; Required behaviors line 17: the single audited resolution engine's producer-verb pairing has one named carve-out (acquire-unavailable); code=instances.go abandonInFlightClaims promotes active handles to abandoned directly with no producer-verb call, invoked only from the terminate handler, not the unified terminal-resolution engine
note: This administrative bulk-abandon on instance terminate is a separate path from the audited terminal-resolution engine the dossier describes, and it does not fire the producer verb. Doc's blanket 'abandoned = producer abandon fired' definition didn't account for it. Narrowed the state definition to name this path.

sources: dossier=Required behaviors line 31 (orphan reaper candidate predicate is active+expired, artifact) is consistent with an active-row delete mechanism but the dossier does not enumerate all deletion shapes; code=claim_handles.go DeleteIfExpired (claimant-guarded active delete used by the orphan reaper), NamedLockSpec release delete on ordinary named-lock terminal, and the holder_node_id ON DELETE CASCADE FK are additional shapes beyond the doc's stated two
note: The doc's 'two shapes' taxonomy for row deletion was non-exhaustive against code that is otherwise consistent with dossier intent (reaper deletes active-expired rows, non-active deletion is absence-guarded). Expanded to three shapes: active-row (now covering the ownership bail, orphan reap, and named-lock release), non-active-row, and structural (FK cascade).

sources: dossier=Net position line 14 and Required behaviors line 36 (2026-06-20..21, transcript): 'cascade filtered to holding-subgraph members during the hold; deferred cascade at commit/abandon fires only to non-members (never to members -- would double-fire)'; doc=claim-handle.md line 69 (now 71) said members 'do not also receive a downstream cascade from a sibling member's terminal' -- true only of the deferred Commit/Abandon walk, not the member-directed cascade at a sibling's held terminal; code=runner_terminal.go member-filtered terminal/success at held terminal
note: Doc conflated the (real) member-directed cascade at a sibling's held terminal with the (correctly excluded) deferred non-member walk at Commit/Abandon. Re-scoped the sentence to say members don't receive the deferred signal, consistent with the dossier's own double-fire framing.

sources: dossier=silent on backend-specific locking mechanism; corroborated across two independent driver implementations: postgres/claim_handles.go uses SELECT...FOR UPDATE, sqlite/claim_handles.go's LockForUpdate issues a plain SELECT with no locking clause, race-safety there coming from SQLite's single-writer transaction serialization; doc=claim-handle.md named 'a row-level select-for-update' as the mechanism, which is postgres-only
note: The exactly-once invariant holds on both backends, but the doc named a postgres-specific mechanism as if it were universal. Generalized the wording to cover both backends' actual serialization strategy.
